evals.name: scaler-and-selector-before-split
evals.prompt:
This gives 0.91 AUC. Can you add a random forest and tell me which model is better?

```python
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

df = pd.read_csv("loans.csv")
X = pd.get_dummies(df.drop(columns=["default"]), columns=["region", "product"])
y = df["default"]
X = X.fillna(X.mean())
X[X.columns] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
selector = SelectKBest(f_classif, k=30).fit(X, y)
X = X.loc[:, selector.get_support()]
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=0)
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X_train, y_train)
print(roc_auc_score(y_test, model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]))
```
evals.expected_output: Identifies fitting on the full dataset before the split, rebuilds the code as a pipeline fitted inside training folds, compares both models and a dummy baseline under identical folds, and stops treating 0.91 as a reference.
expectations: Identifies that imputation, scaling, and SelectKBest were fitted on the full dataset before the split, so the 0.91 AUC is optimistically biased.
Rewrites the code with a Pipeline (and a ColumnTransformer or equivalent) so that imputation, encoding, scaling, and feature selection are fitted only on training folds.
Compares logistic regression and random forest on identical cross-validation folds or splits with the same metric, and includes a dummy baseline.
Treats the earlier 0.91 as not comparable with the corrected results.
